questions.text: What does Mrs Bello do for a living?
options: She sells thread on the street.
questions.instruction: Lagos wakes early. Long before the sun is high, street sellers set up their stalls, buses queue at the junctions, and workers hurry towards the ferry. Mrs Bello, a tailor, has run her small shop on the same street for twenty years. She says the noise no longer troubles her; she treats it as the city's heartbeat. What worries her more is the rising price of thread and cloth, which has forced her to raise her charges twice this year.

questions.text: What did Efe do when the power failed?
options: She sat quietly in the dark.
She asked everyone to hold up their torches.
questions.instruction: When the power failed in the school hall, the students sat in darkness. Rather than panic, the head girl, Efe, asked everyone to switch on their torches and hold them up. Within seconds the hall glowed like a field of stars, and the assembly carried on. The principal later praised her calm thinking.
